item.title: Spain: Madrid mourns train crash victims as rescuers work through the night
item.description: Spain reels from the deadly Toledo high-speed train collision that killed 68 and injured more than 100, sparking grief, protests and calls for resignations.

item.title: Support for UN vote to end US embargo on Cuba falls to 30-year low
item.description: Similar resolutions have been approved almost every year since 1992, but usually by overwhelming margins.

item.title: Belgium's finance and tax agency hit by cyberattack
item.description: The online portal MyMinfin and several other services have been temporarily taken offline as a precaution while officials investigate and secure their systems.

item.title: Fed holds rates days before US midterms as two officials push for another hike
item.description: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged on Wednesday, six days before the midterms, but two officials, including Governor Lisa Cook, whom US President Donald Trump is trying to fire, voted for a hike, with inflation at 3.7% and investors still braced for a rise in December.

item.title: UEFA reschedules Europa League match amid planned French general strike
item.description: UEFA has brought forward kick-off to 4.30pm on Wednesday 4 November because of a general strike called by French unions the next day.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 28th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 28th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: ‘Inexplicable’ order by control centre investigated after Spain train crash
item.description: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said that "the whole of Spain is in mourning" following the accident and expressed his solidarity with the victims, their families and the injured.

item.title: Poland chosen to host €227m Patriot missile maintenance centre
item.description: Poland has been chosen to host Europe's service centre for PAC-3 missiles used in Patriot systems. It will be the only such facility outside the US.

item.title: 60.000 runners, two million spectators, one city: New York gets ready for marathon day
item.description: New York will become the running capital of the world this Sunday. On November 1, nearly 60,000 people will line up at the start of the NYC Marathon, one of the world’s most iconic races. But what’s getting people running?

item.title: From Baku’s old city to mud volcanoes: discovering Azerbaijan’s wonders
item.description: Azerbaijan is a country rich in history, culture, and natural wonders. In this episode of Grand Voyager, Lilly Douse explores Baku’s historic Old City, discovers the ancient rock carvings of Gobustan and visits the region's mud volcanoes.

item.title: EU approves €319 million in state aid to Austrian 'first of a kind' next generation semiconductor factory
item.description: The European Commission has approved Austria’s state-aid grant to Infineon Technologies to upgrade its existing semiconductor facility in Villach, Carinthia, and make it the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for next generation semiconductors.

item.title: Nord Stream pipeline won't reopen after the war, Brussels tells the US and Russia
item.description: Brussels insists Nord Stream will remain shut after the war in Ukraine ends, countering a joint push by the US and Russia to restart the pipeline.

item.title: Spain: Rescuers search mangled train wreckage near Toledo
item.description: At least 68 people have been killed and dozens more injured after two high-speed trains collided near Urda, in central Spain’s Toledo province, on Wednesday, 28 October. Authorities warned the toll could rise further as rescuers searched the wreckage.

item.title: Hungary’s €5.4bn defence loan approved as EU wraps first SAFE round
item.description: The European Commission has approved Hungary’s €5.4 billion defence loan application, completing the first round of SAFE allocations and leaving just over €21 billion available for a new funding round.

item.title: European gas price crosses €100 for first time since 2022 as EU warns of new crisis
item.description: Europe's benchmark gas price crossed €100 per megawatt-hour on Wednesday afternoon for the first time since the 2022 energy crisis, just hours after EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen warned that Europe faces "another energy crisis" and a difficult winter.

item.title: Discovering the birthplace of apples in Kazakhstan’s wild forests
item.description: In this episode of Modern Nomads, we head to southern Kazakhstan to uncover the birthplace of apples.

item.title: EU removes mention of ‘associate membership’ from Canada declaration
item.description: The EU has dropped “associate membership” from the draft EU-Canada summit declaration after German objections, replacing it with “ever closer association”.

item.title: EU and Canada explore LNG deal as Europe grapples with gas crisis
item.description: A draft EU-Canada summit statement envisages a feasibility study on long-term LNG exports to Europe as Brussels seeks to diversify its energy supplies. But questions remain over infrastructure, costs and the impact on the bloc's climate ambitions.

item.title: Satellites the size of drinks cans: Young engineers take on a space challenge in Uzbekistan
item.description: From classroom calculations to rocket launches, teams from 15 countries tested their creations under real flight conditions. Equipped with sensors and communication systems, the devices collected data before descending by parachute.

item.title: Germany and Japan strengthen economic ties as global tensions rise
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi agreed in Tokyo on Wednesday to deepen cooperation on economic security and high tech. It is Merz's first visit to Japan since taking office in May 2025.

item.title: South Korea fines Google, Apple for pushing app developers onto their payment systems
item.description: South Korea has fined Google and Apple a combined 63.7 billion won (€42.7m), for steering app developers towards their in-house payment systems and holding up app reviews, adding to a string of penalties the US tech giants face over app store rules, including in the EU.

item.title: More than half of pilots say they flew while tired as trust in reporting systems remains low, survey finds
item.description: Pilot fatigue remains a major aviation concern, with many reporting nodding off during flights instead of declaring themselves unfit to fly.

item.title: UK budget: Here’s five key takeaways from the Chancellor’s speech
item.description: The UK's new Chancellor, John Healey, has delivered his first Budget in the role. Here's five key takeaways from his speech.

item.title: Pictures show rescue efforts after deadly Spain train collision
item.description: Images from central Spain show the wreckage and rescue efforts after two high-speed trains collided near Toledo, killing at least 64 people and injuring dozens more.

item.title: Trump rolls back methane rules for US oil and gas industry
item.description: Trump is seeking to lower energy costs ahead of next week's midterm elections, as rising oil prices linked to the US war with Iran fuel voter frustration.

item.title: Biometrics, AI and digital passports: Europeans ‘most cautious’ about travel technology, IATA survey finds
item.description: European travellers are the least enthusiastic when it comes to using a digital passport, according to IATA’s 2026 Global Passenger Survey. The research also found how digital privacy concerns and entry requirements are shaping the way people are travelling.

item.title: Using artificial intelligence to step up the fight against doping
item.description: Tools used by WADA and national bodies, the danger that would-be cheats use them too, the personal data risk from a simple online post, and lessons from the "Santorini Summit".

item.title: EU defence chief warns of fuel crunch if Europe goes to war
item.description: The European Commissioner for Defence, Andrius Kubilius, has warned that Europe must be prepared to "surge" energy production to fuel its armies in conflict.

item.title: Europe needs more oil refineries to weather energy shocks, EU warns
item.description: The European Commission is treating the loss of refining capacity as a vulnerability that Europe can no longer afford to ignore.

item.title: Gene therapy beyond rare diseases with Alessandra Biffi | Euronews Tech Talks
item.description: After decades developing gene therapies for ultra-rare conditions, Alessandra Biffi is researching how altering a patient’s DNA could help treat more common diseases like diabetes.

item.title: Palme d'Or-winning Iranian director Jafar Panahi facing five-year prison term in new ruling
item.description: The latest ruling follows a December 2025 conviction for “propaganda activities against the regime”, which carried a one-year prison sentence and two-year travel ban.

item.title: EU begins talks on tougher safeguards for newcomers, with Montenegro first in line
item.description: EU governments are divided over proposed safeguards for future members, including a 15-year probation period and the possible suspension of voting rights, as Montenegro becomes the test case for tougher enlargement rules.

item.title: Evacuation or forced deportation: where will trapped citizens of Russia-occupied Oleshky go?
item.description: A temporary ceasefire opened the way for aid and civilian evacuations from Russian-occupied Oleshky. But reports that residents could be transported through Russia or Moscow-occupied Crimea have raised concerns over whether they will be able to reach Ukrainian-controlled territory.

item.title: Checking luggage with Ryanair? Airline announces earlier baggage drop deadline
item.description: Europe’s largest airline made the change to ensure customers have more time to clear airport security and passport control.

item.title: The British Library is exploring the mysterious world of Agatha Christie — but how much do you already know?
item.description: Don your best tweed and twirl your moustache — there's a quiz afoot.

item.title: Space Industries opens Stellar Hub in Turin, one of Europe's largest satellite factories
item.description: In Settimo Torinese, Stellar Hub has been inaugurated, an 8,000-square-metre facility for mass-producing satellites of up to 600 kilograms, with a 2,000-square-metre clean room among the largest in Europe.

item.title: Black Friday or Travel Tuesday? How to secure the best deals on hotels and flights in 2026
item.description: We might not celebrate Thanksgiving in Europe, but that doesn’t mean you can’t snag yourself a holiday bargain this November.

item.title: Social media on trial again: Meta and Snap face jury over alleged harm to teens
item.description: The latest case is a sign of the mounting legal pushback around the world against the alleged harms of social media to users, especially children and teens.

item.title: Spain: First footage reveals wreckage of deadly high-speed train crash
item.description: At least 10 people died when a high-speed train struck another near Toledo, Spain. Two carriages derailed, leaving rescuers searching through the wreckage as authorities warned the death toll could rise.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami after fleeing Brazil
item.description: On Monday, Bolsonaro described the travel ban as an attempt to intimidate him, insisting he had no plans to leave Brazil.

item.title: First aerial images show scene of deadly train crash in Toledo, Spain
item.description: Aerial footage shows the aftermath of a collision between two high-speed trains near Urda, in Spain's Toledo province, as emergency crews continue rescue and response operations.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 28th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 28th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: BNP Paribas downplays French debt exposure as stock trading lifts profit
item.description: The French multinational bank BNP Paribas beat profit forecasts in the third quarter as revenue from equities trading surged 50%, and announced a €1.3 billion share buyback while playing down its exposure to French debt.

item.title: Abandon ship! Around 200 ‘cruise for life’ passengers stranded in Cambodia
item.description: US-based operator Villa Vie Residences has suspended operations due to an ‘extraordinary’ rise in fuel costs since the Iran war began.

item.title: Small and very scary: Rare miniature T.rex dinosaur skeleton fetches €42 million at auction
item.description: A dinosaur that looks like a tiny Tyrannosaurus rex is now one of the world's most expensive fossils having been sold at a Sotheby's auction for €42.6 million in New York.

item.title: Has the White House tipped rapper Nicki Minaj as Donald Trump's new press secretary?
item.description: Rapper Nicki Minaj appeared with Trump at a recent rally in Michigan, where he made a comment about her “beautiful” and “hard to miss” butt. Now there's even talk of a possible job at the White House for the MAGA-loving rapper.

item.title: Cross-border network helps EU workers abroad claim wages and benefits
item.description: A cross-border network of counsellors, funded by the EU, is helping Europeans who work in other member states to claim the wages and social rights they are entitled to.

item.title: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 68, injures more than 100
item.description: The collision occured in central Spanish province of Toledo, south of Madrid. Officials say that the crash was caused by human error after a computer system failure. Rail service is now suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia.

item.title: 'Dead Poets Society' sells out eight consecutive months at Teatro da Trindade
item.description: The stage version of the film that captivated generations is sold out at Teatro da Trindade until the end of the year, before touring nationwide.

item.title: Mao meme comments won't 'cause serious economic problems' for Mbappé, says expert
item.description: Sports journalist Ken Early said Kylian Mbappé was probably “as surprised as anybody” after a joke involving a meme depicting the Real Madrid forward as Mao Zedong sparked a reaction by China.
